meta.notes: Segment 3: TED-Ed glue vs tape verdict beat (HHuTrcXNxOk, 03:05-03:15). This is a code-drawn reconstruction of the beat's composition and timing from flat vector shapes. It is NOT a pixel copy of the hand-drawn original, and nothing here should be read as pixel-identical. Gaps: (1) meta.fps is 24 because the scene schema types fps as an integer and the renderer probes r_frame_rate as fps/1; the reference is 23.976 fps, so after 240 frames the two timelines differ by about 0.24 frame. (2) The 240-frame reference clip (refs/seg3-glue-tape-240f.webm) shows a crowd scene for roughly the first 100 frames and then the two flexing characters on a blue platform; it contains no anvil, no bowling balls and no verdict label, so those elements come from the brief and the lesson text, not from reference frames, and the clip start does not yet align with 03:05. (3) The glue bottle and tape roll are original flat-vector characters with their own proportions and faces, not copies of the original drawings; there is no hand-drawn character library in the engine. (4) The background wash is three flat ellipses, not the textured wash of the original. (5) Palette entries with a source number were sampled from storyboard frame f08 (about reference frame 168); the others are authored. (6) Label font is the fixture Liberation Sans Bold, not the original lettering. Beat timing is authored: platform f0-12, characters f4-18, beam f18-34, glue blob f40-52, anvil drops f52-72, tape strip f40-52, three balls pop at f60/72/84, fists pulse f100-124, verdict pill f132-140, verdict words from f140 (3 frame stagger), still from f185 to f239.
